source_text:
Λέγει μοι: Ἁπλότητα ἔχε καὶ ἄκακος γίνου, καὶ ἔσῃ ὡς τὰ νήπια τὰ μὴ γινώσκοντα τὴν πονηρίαν τὴν ἀπολλύουσαν τὴν ζωὴν τῶν ἀνθρώπων.
πρῶτον μὲν μηδενὸς καταλάλει μηδὲ ἡδέως ἄκουε καταλαλοῦντος: εἰ δὲ μή, καὶ σὺ ὁ ἀκούων ἔνοχος ἔσῃ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ καταλαλοῦντος, ἐὰν πιστεύσῃς τῇ καταλαλιᾷ ᾗ ἂν ἀκούσῃς: πιστεύσας γὰρ καὶ σὺ αὐτὸς ἕξεις κατὰ τοῦ ἀδελφοῦ σου: οὕτως οὖν ἔνοχος ἔσῃ τῆς ἁμαρτίας τοῦ καταλαλοῦντος.
πονηρὰ ἡ καταλαλιά: ἀκατάστατον δαιμόνιόν ἐστιν, μηδέποτε εἰρηνεῦον, ἀλλὰ πάντοτε ἐν διχοστασίαις κατοικοῦν. ἀπέχου οὖν ἀπ’ αὐτοῦ, καὶ εὐθηνίαν πάντοτε ἕξεις μετὰ πάντων.
ἔνδυσαι δὲ τὴν σεμνότητα, ἐν ᾗ οὐδὲν πρόσκομμά ἐστιν πονηρόν, ἀλλὰ πάντα ὁμαλὰ καὶ ἱλαρά. ἐργάζου τὸ ἀγαθὸν καὶ ἐκ τῶν κόπων σου ὧν ὁ θεὸς δίδωσίν σοι πᾶσιν ὑστερουμένοις δίδου ἁπλῶς, μὴ διστάζων, τίνι δῷς ἢ τίνι μὴ δῷς. πᾶσιν δίδου: πᾶσιν γάρ ὁ θεὸς δίδοσθαι θέλει ἐκ τῶν ἰδίων δωρημάτων.
οἱ οὖν λαμβάνοντες ἀποδώσουσιν λόγον τῷ θεῷ, διατί ἔλαβον καὶ εἰς τί: οἱ μὲν γὰρ λαμβάνοντες θλιβόμενοι οὐ δικασθήσονται, οἱ δὲ ἐν ὑποκρίσει λαμβάνοντες τίσουσιν δίκην.
ὁ οὖν διδοὺς ἀθῷός ἐστιν: ὡς γὰρ ἔλαβεν παρὰ τοῦ κυρίου τὴν διακονίαν τελέσαι, ἁπλῶς αὐτὴν ἐτέλεσεν, μηθὲν διακρίνων, τίνι δῷ ἢ μὴ δῷ. ἐγένετο οὖν ἡ διακονία αὕτη ἁπλῶς τελεσθεῖσα ἔνδοξος παρὰ τῷ θεῷ. ὁ οὖν οὕτως ἁπλῶς διακονῶν τῷ θεῷ ζήσεται.
φύλασσε οὖν τὴν ἐντολὴν ταύτην, ὥς σοι λελάληκα, ἵνα ἡ μετάνοιά σου καὶ τοῦ οἴκου σου ἐν ἁπλότητι εὑρεθῇ, καὶ ἀκακία καθαρὰ καὶ ἀμίαντος.
orientation: The Shepherd gives Hermas the second commandment. It is about simplicity: slander no one, and give to all who are in need without picking and choosing.
pass_a_gloss: He says to me: Have simplicity and become innocent, and you will be like the infants who do not know the wickedness that destroys the life of men. First of all, speak evil of no one, and do not listen gladly to one who speaks evil; but if not, you also, the one hearing, will be guilty of the sin of the one who speaks evil, if you believe the slander which you hear; for having believed, you also yourself will have something against your brother; thus therefore you will be guilty of the sin of the one who speaks evil. Slander is evil; it is a restless demon, never making peace, but always dwelling in divisions. Keep away therefore from it, and you will always have prosperity with all. But put on reverence, in which there is no evil stumbling block, but all things are smooth and cheerful. Work the good, and from your labors which God gives to you, give simply to all who are in need, not doubting to whom you should give or to whom you should not give. Give to all; for God wishes gifts to be given to all from his own gifts. Those therefore who receive will give an account to God, why they received and for what; for those who receive while afflicted will not be judged, but those who receive in hypocrisy will pay the penalty. The one therefore who gives is innocent; for as he received from the Lord the ministry to complete, he completed it simply, making no distinction to whom he should give or should not give. This ministry therefore, completed simply, became glorious before God. The one therefore who serves God thus simply will live. Keep therefore this commandment, as I have spoken to you, so that your repentance and that of your household may be found in simplicity, and pure and undefiled innocence.

choices.why: Glossary term; the fixed rendering for the virtue of single-hearted generosity and innocence.
Renders the quality of being without evil, paired with simplicity in the commandment.
The noun form of speaking evil against someone; 'slander' captures the destructive speech.
Renders the dignified, holy character that has no evil stumbling block.
Adverbial form of the glossary term simplicity, keeping the same root in English.
Noun form matching the adjective 'innocent' used earlier, keeping the same root.

pass_b_english: The Shepherd said to me, “Hold to simplicity and be innocent, and you will be like little children, who do not know the wickedness that destroys human life.

“First, slander no one, and take no pleasure in listening to a slanderer. Otherwise you, the listener, will also be guilty of the slanderer’s sin, if you believe the slander you hear. For once you believe it, you too will hold something against your brother. In this way, then, you will be guilty of the slanderer’s sin.
“Slander is evil. It is a restless demon, never at peace, always living amid divisions. So keep away from it, and things will always go well between you and everyone.

“Put on reverence. In reverence there is nothing evil to stumble over. Everything is smooth and cheerful. Do what is good, and from the fruit of your labor, which God gives you, give with simplicity to all who are in need. Do not hesitate over whom you should give to and whom you should not. Give to all, for God wants everyone to be given a share of his own gifts.

“Those who receive will give an account to God of why they took and for what purpose. Those who take because they are hard pressed will not be judged. But those who take under false pretenses will pay the penalty.

“So the giver is guiltless. For he received from the Lord a ministry to carry out, and he carried it out with simplicity, making no distinction about whom to give to and whom not. So this ministry, carried out with simplicity, became glorious in the sight of God. Whoever serves with simplicity in this way will live to God.
“Keep this commandment, then, as I have spoken it to you, so that your repentance and the repentance of your household may be found in simplicity, and your innocence pure and undefiled.”

problems.quote: Give to everyone, for God wants gifts from his own bounty to be given to everyone.
problems.why: Seems to encourage indiscriminate giving, but next sentence says recipients are judged; tension unresolved.
problems.fix: Clarify: give without discriminating, but God will judge recipients' use of gifts.

edits.old: Give to everyone, for God wants gifts from his own bounty to be given to everyone.
edits.new: Give to everyone, for God wants gifts from his own bounty to be given to everyone, without distinction.

fixed: The English already says what the source says: 'Give to everyone, for God wants gifts from his own bounty to be given to everyone.' The following sentence about recipients being judged is also present, so the tension is in the source itself, not a mistranslation. I added 'without distinction' to make the intended sense clearer without changing the meaning.

problems.why: Three overlapping terms for saved community used inconsistently; reader cannot tell if these are identical groups or distinct categories.
problems.fix: Clarify in intro whether these are synonyms or distinct groups in Hermas's theology.

problems.quote: give simply to all who are in need, not doubting to whom you should give or to whom you should not give
problems.why: 'Simply' translates haplos but may mislead as 'in a simple manner'; context requires 'generously' or 'without discrimination.'
problems.fix: Use 'generously' or 'without reservation' to match context of indiscriminate charity.

edits.old: give simply to all who are in need, not doubting to whom you should give or to whom you should not give
edits.new: give generously to all who are in need, not doubting to whom you should give or to whom you should not give

fixed: The glossary problem about 'the elect' is not a translation issue in this section; the source text does not use the term 'the elect' here, so no edit is needed.

The mistranslation problem is real: the source uses 'ἁπλῶς' (haplōs) in the context of indiscriminate giving, which the glossary defines as 'simplicity' but here means 'generously' or 'without discrimination.' The English 'simply' misleads as 'in a simple manner.' Changed to 'generously' to match the context of indiscriminate charity.

polish.changed: Clarified speaker attribution and pronoun references, smoothed sentence rhythm for reading aloud, and removed the redundant phrase 'without distinction' at the end of the fourth paragraph to resolve the apparent tension with the following judgment on recipients.

last_rejected.why: Glossary requires 'simplicity' for ἁπλότης; 'simply' is adverb form used consistently for ἁπλῶς. But the glossary fixes 'simplicity' as the English for ἁπλότης. The adverb ἁπλῶς derives from ἁπλότης. 'Simply' is natural English adverb; not a glossary violation.
last_rejected.ruling: ἁπλῶς is adverbial form of ἁπλότης; 'simply' is correct English adverb, not a glossary violation for the noun.
